name: Aztec Fluids & Machinery Limited
summary:
Research hold, not a clean compounder or a purchase recommendation. Aztec has a useful industrial printer, consumables and service franchise, but pre-IPO parent returns do not describe the acquired group. FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹96.53 crore, PAT ₹7.41 crore and normalized operating ROIC about 14.4%. Printer revenue fell 12.45% while recurring consumables grew near 20%.
At the 19 October 2026 close of ₹104.80, market capitalization is ₹142.53 crore. BQS is 4.94, displayed 4.9/10; GQS is 5.60, displayed 5.6/10. IAS and R are NS. A conditional, cash-funded base produces about 11.1% five-year IRR versus the common 15% hurdle, but legal status, supplier renewal and implementation evidence are insufficient for a supported ordinary base case.
Positive group cash flow, consumables demand and restoration of Jet's bank status are real counterweights. The decisive concerns are supplier dependence, modest acquisition returns, inventory and aged assets, substantially higher approved promoter-pay ceilings, an adverse customs order with unresolved current status, and coarse SME-lot execution. An administrative tax finding is not a criminal conviction. The missing contingent-note reconciliation is not established concealment. [S1–S13; M1–M3]

sections.text:
Research hold, not a clean compounder or a purchase recommendation. Aztec has a useful industrial printer, consumables and service franchise, but pre-IPO parent returns do not describe the acquired group. FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹96.53 crore, PAT ₹7.41 crore and normalized operating ROIC about 14.4%. Printer revenue fell 12.45% while recurring consumables grew near 20%.

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Cutoff: 20 October 2026. Quote: 19 October 2026. Equity hurdle: 15% nominal INR. Financial amounts are INR crore unless stated. Exact legal entity: Aztec Fluids & Machinery Limited; BSE SME 544177 / AZTEC; ISIN INE0SCB01016. Incorporated 28 April 2010; converted from private to public on 18 November 2023. The NSE interoperability master verifies the security but does not make this an NSE-listed stock. Board lot is 1,000 shares; issued shares are 13,600,000. The ₹5 lakh reference is a research convention, not the user's proposed investment.
Accounts follow Indian AS under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, not Ind AS. Parent FY21–FY26 is the comparable growth series. Consolidated FY25 includes Jet from 31 May 2024; FY26 includes a full year. No six-year group history is manufactured. The latest audited balance sheet is 31 March 2026; October cash and debt are forecast, not observed.
G1 Integrity: Hold. G2 Reliability: Conditional. G3 Funding: Hold. G4 Tradability: Hold. Nine quality factors have Medium confidence; R and L have Low confidence and are NS. BQS/GQS remain conditionally comparison-eligible because G2 is not a demonstrated central financial-reliability failure. Funding Hold alone does not erase business-quality rankings. A later material reliability finding would require withdrawal of both rankings. [S1–S6; M1–M5]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors, each assigned once: GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 6, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 5, BAL 4, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P 4, L NS. The audit records two or more material facts, contrary evidence, confidence and evidence IDs for each factor. Unknowns are not scored 5.
BQS: GOV 0.80 + MOAT 1.00 + REV 0.72 + DUR 0.60 + CAP 0.60 + CASH 0.50 + BAL 0.32 + EXEC 0.40 = 4.94; display 4.9; coverage 100%. GQS: REV 2.40 + DUR 1.20 + EARN 0.75 + CAP 0.75 + CASH 0.50 = 5.60; display 5.6; coverage 100%. No governance cap applies: GOV is 4 and G1 is not an established severe failure.
IAS uses unrounded BQS: Q 1.235 + D 0.60 + P 0.40 = 2.235 known contribution. R has 35% missing weight and L 10%; coverage is 55%. The missing-data bound is 2.685–6.735, not a score or confidence interval. Raw/final IAS is NS. Naively applying the R schedule to conditional 11.05% IRR gives R 4, but that is deliberately not adopted. A demonstrated actual funding failure would cap any then-computable IAS at 3. [Factor audit; score audit]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
Aztec supplies industrial coding and marking printers, inks, makeup/wash fluids, spares and after-sales service for production lines. Its range includes CIJ, TTO, DOD, NIJ and laser technologies. It is neither an office-printer commodity distributor nor a proven owner of every core printer technology. The RHP describes imported Lead Tech printers/components, local assembly/testing and cartridge-design IP. Fluidtech, a promoter partnership, supplies inks and consumables under a 2023 agreement. Jet adds ink manufacturing and regional distribution.
FY26 group revenue: assembled printers ₹24.6561 crore (25.54%); makeup/wash ₹37.9522 (39.32%); traded ink ₹20.3853 (21.12%); AMC/repairs ₹4.2968 (4.45%); spares/other ₹9.1742 (9.50%); export drawback ₹0.0658. Accounting labels do not prove that every product is proprietary manufacture. Repeat purchases are valuable but are not guaranteed subscriptions.
FY23's largest customer represented 35.01% of revenue and the top ten 57.11%; the top ten were 65.36% in 9MFY24. Firm long-term customer contracts were not in place. Current concentration is ND. Management's FY26 claim of 8,000+ installed products and 4,000+ customers is not a verified active-printer cohort or retention measure. Historical pipes/fittings concentration is material; an inconsistent percentage label in the RHP is not used to fabricate a precise current mix. [S1 note 21; S4 business and risk factors]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
A supported printer on a production line can generate repeat consumables, spares and service. Formulation compatibility, cartridge identification and the cost of downtime create useful switching friction. The RHP cites two cartridge-design patents and PCB anti-counterfeit identification. These support a narrow application/service advantage, not proven industry-wide pricing power, dominant market share or a software network effect.
Lead Tech is both an advantage and a dependency. The RHP says exclusivity, in place since 2015, runs to 6 December 2026 and is renewable by mutual discretion. No executed extension was located by the cutoff. Product modification requires supplier approval; responsibilities include service and sales targets. A 1,200-CIJ-printer target for 2022 was missed without repercussion. RHP FY23 imports were 78.58% of material consumption; Lead Tech Group was 68.22% of 9MFY24 procurement. Continued distribution is not ownership of the underlying technology.
The four-company economic comparator set is deliberate. Control Print is the closest Indian listed coding/consumables business and has larger manufacturing and service scale. Videojet has a much larger global installed footprint. Domino combines Brother-backed technology, manufacturing and aftermarket support. Markem-Imaje/Dover already offers commercial coding and traceability software. Their global parent valuations are not comparable pure-play multiples. Laser migration and third-party alternatives may reduce some ink demand. MOAT 5 reflects useful but contestable advantages. [S4; P1–P6]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Comparable parent revenue from FY21 through FY26 was ₹33.8994, ₹45.7155, ₹54.2611, ₹67.6802, ₹73.8709 and ₹83.3781 crore. The preferred five-year CAGR is 19.72%; three-year CAGR is 15.40%. Annual growth was 34.86%, 18.69%, 24.73%, 9.15% and 12.87%. Consolidated FY25 revenue of ₹88.4249 crore became ₹96.5304 crore in FY26, up 9.17%. Jet's acquisition timing and eliminations prevent treating this as an organic six-year group series.
REV starts at 7 for a comparable five-year CAGR between 15% and 20%. A single minus-one adjustment reflects two slower fiscal years and weak new-printer revenue; final REV is 6. There is no additional small-base penalty. FY26 category growth: printers −12.45%; makeup/wash +20.76%; ink +19.68%; AMC +48.18%; spares +3.69%. The current business is generating more repeat sales while hardware revenue contracts. Current units versus pricing are ND.
Historical printer unit sales of 664, 853 and 971 in FY21–FY23, with approximate realized ASPs of ₹1.64, ₹1.70 and ₹1.745 lakh, establish earlier physical growth. They cannot be rolled forward to invent FY26 units. Manufacturing, packaging and coding demand provide a market, but the global chemicals or packaging TAM is not Aztec's accessible revenue pool. [S1–S4; growth_drivers.json]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Plausible growth avenues are additional active printers, higher consumable usage and attachment, Jet's regional coverage and selected local components. AZTRACE was launched on 10 September 2026, but paid cohorts, ARR, churn, implementation costs and recurring contracts are ND. It receives no separate software multiple. Unreconciled backlog claims are not used as binding demand.
The bottom-up driver file starts from audited revenue categories and uses clearly labeled indices, not fictitious absolute units. Base printer units +8% and ASP +2% imply 10.16% growth. Consumable active base +7%, usage +1% and price +2% imply 10.23%. Service attachment +5%, usage +3% and price +2% imply 10.31%. The cash model rounds this down to 10% overall growth, conditional on supplier continuity. Bull growth of 16% requires faster unit/base expansion. FY26 printer contraction is the important contrary evidence.
Base assumptions are an 11.2% operating EBIT margin, cash capex of 4.5% of sales, D&A of 2.3%, unchanged operating-working-capital ratios and no dividends. The model reaches ₹163.87 crore revenue and ₹58.54 crore ONWC in October 2031, versus audited opening ONWC of ₹34.4828 crore. Cash capex including the forecast stub totals ₹31.79 crore. It is funded by operating cash and existing mutual funds, not a fictional undrawn line.
Current development assets of ₹6.318 crore and FY26 cash capex of ₹6.435 crore are recognized. Capacity/utilization and new-product qualification are insufficiently reconciled for an absolute unit-based ceiling; claimed daily capacities are not treated as verified throughput. The growth/reinvestment/incremental-return identity is a sanity check, not a reliable forecast in a changing acquired perimeter. [S1; S4; S12–S13; model]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Pulin Vaidhya and Amisha Vaidhya lead a family-controlled business, with Kumudchandra Vaidhya also on the board. The AGM's 10,167,600 interested shares abstaining from remuneration RPT votes corroborate about 74.76% control against 13,600,000 issued shares. Latest primary pledge data are not independently verified. FY26 RPTs include Fluidtech purchases of ₹8.1224 crore and Axis Druckfarben sales of ₹6.4869 crore and purchases of ₹1.1448 crore. Axis receivables were ₹1.4737 crore; Fluidtech payables ₹1.3828 crore. These require scrutiny of terms and collection, not an automatic accusation of abuse.
Audited FY26 pay was ₹1.20 crore to Pulin and ₹0.90 crore to Amisha, plus ₹0.043 crore sitting fees. AGM items 3 and 5 approved annual ceilings of ₹3.50 crore each, supported by 450,000 public votes with interested shares abstaining. A ceiling is not actual pay or an unavoidable fixed commitment. The AGM summary's prior-pay figure for Amisha differs from the audited financial note; the latter is used for actual FY26 pay. Full utilization would add ₹4.90 crore annually. The downside model tests persistence beyond the approved term as a hypothetical renewal, not a verified obligation. Rental ceilings of ₹0.15 crore each also exceed historical combined rent of ₹0.126 crore.
Customs order dated 31 October 2025 is a serious adverse administrative finding. IEC 0813008310, addresses and promoter match the RHP entity. The case concerns 2016–2020 imports and the 24 February 2021 SCN. Aztec denied the allegations, citing favorable CESTAT and appellate classification decisions for the same models, computer-connectivity evidence and objections to adjudication while the Gujarat HC quashing order remained operative. The Supreme Court's 22 January 2026 batch order remanded CA10782/2024 to the High Court for remaining contentions; it is not a final merits win or proof that the customs order is stayed. Later appeal, stay, payment and deposit status remain ND. Earlier sanctioned refunds of ₹3.919 crore are not automatically credits against this later order.
Execution milestones are mixed: Jet acquired on 31 May 2024, but FY26 Jet PAT was only ₹0.261 crore; an August 2025 guarantee-related NPA classification was addressed through February 2026 guarantee approval and March regularization; AZTRACE launched, but commercial conversion is unverified. KARMA & Co LLP's opinion was unmodified and the audit trail was reported operational. These counterweights support GOV 4 / G1 Hold rather than an assertion of criminal fraud or severe minority diversion. [S1–S12]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Earnings normalization: Group FY25/FY26 PAT was ₹7.5640/₹7.4071 crore. EBIT equals PBT plus interest-only cost minus other income, leaving bank charges as operating costs: ₹8.5420/₹10.7409 crore. Economic EBITDA was ₹9.7286/₹12.9390 crore. Management's FY26 EBITDA of ₹13.9578 crore includes other income and all finance-cost addbacks; the definitions are not interchangeable. Other income fell from ₹2.8696 to ₹0.8670 crore. FY25 included mutual-fund gains of ₹1.0516 crore, FX gains of ₹0.9464 crore and refund income of ₹0.3629 crore. FY26 balance writebacks of ₹0.3849 crore and provision reversals of ₹0.1100 crore are not recurring sales. Warranty expense fell from ₹1.5066 to ₹0.1369 crore, contributing substantially to EBIT growth. Goodwill amortization of ₹0.4702 crore and development amortization of ₹0.3446 crore are explicit costs.
Cash: The FY26 cash-flow face reports CFO of ₹8.5354 crore and adds FD interest income of ₹0.2387 crore rather than subtracting it. The chairman's CFO of ₹8.0581 crore and CFI of −₹9.2704 crore reconcile the approximate ₹0.4773 crore classification difference against the face CFI of −₹9.7477 crore; total cash movement is unchanged. The model uses adjusted CFO while retaining the face value. FY25 CFO was ₹5.8519 crore. Two-year group CFO/PAT is 0.929; cash capex was ₹6.1477/₹6.4350 crore, leaving aggregate FCF of ₹1.3273 crore. Parent three-year CFO/PAT of 0.404 includes advances to Jet and is not equivalent to group collection failure. RHP FY23 restated PAT/CFO of ₹3.2738/₹4.4784 crore are kept separate from original audited ₹3.1922/₹4.0876 crore.
Working capital: FY26 inventory was ₹32.1330 crore, up ₹9.3479 crore; receivables ₹27.3285 crore, up ₹2.3868 crore; payables ₹24.1979 crore, up ₹8.8830 crore. End-balance DSO was 103.34 days; inventory/sales 121.50 days; payables/sales 91.50 days. The last two are sales-based intensity measures, not cost-based DIO/DPO. Disputed receivables of ₹3.8303 crore remain classified good; total receivables older than three years are ₹4.7777 crore. No unsupported recovery or full write-off is assumed. Supplier financing can reverse, and working capital is deducted once in the cash model.
Capital: Funding-side IC equals equity plus debt less cash, mutual funds and the non-operating corporate loan. FY25/FY26 IC is ₹52.1566/₹59.8533 crore, including goodwill, development, restricted FDs and acquisition capital. FY26 NOPAT at 25% tax is ₹8.0557 crore; average IC ₹56.0050 crore; ROIC 14.38%. Including the ₹4.9449 crore corporate loan in total deployed capital reduces the return to about 13.22%. One-year incremental ROIC is 21.43%, not a proven through-cycle rate. Estimated WACC is 13.5% using 80% equity at 15% plus 20% debt at 10% after 25% tax; an 11.5–15.5% range shows the excess return is not robust. Historical parent returns of roughly 23–33% are not extrapolated after acquisition.
Claims: Debt is ₹16.6961 crore, including ₹15.4339 crore revolving/short-term funding and ₹1.2622 crore term debt, of which ₹0.3522 crore is current. Cash of ₹0.1912 crore less ₹0.0106 crore dividend ringfence leaves ₹0.1806 crore. Mutual funds of ₹9.2347 crore are a modeled liquidation source, not bank cash; fund types, redemption terms and current NAV need verification. Restricted FDs of ₹4.5396 crore are not freely netted. ONWC, taxes, gratuity, warranty and deposits are mapped. The ₹10.7754 crore parent-to-Jet loan and ₹7.65 crore subsidiary guarantee are not added twice to consolidated debt.
Disclosed GST/TDS contingencies are ₹0.3457 crore net of pre-deposits. The customs order's nominal company amounts total ₹7.0571094 crore plus unquantified interest; a ₹0.50 crore deposit credit is unresolved. The ₹27.493 crore goods valuation and personal/broker penalties are not extra company cash claims. Current enforceability and payment status are not established. [S1–S9; history and claims files]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Entry equity value is ₹104.80 × 1.36 crore shares = ₹142.528 crore. Using the last audited group figures gives reported P/E 19.24x and P/B 2.48x. EV after usable cash and mutual funds, but not restricted FDs, is ₹149.8088 crore: 13.95x economic EBIT or 11.58x economic EBITDA. This excludes the unresolved customs claim and gives no free-cash credit to the corporate loan. These are March-based balance adjustments to an October quote.
The monthly model starts on 31 March 2026, forecasts the 202-day stub to the quote, then runs five years to 19 October 2031. It includes operating cash, interest, tax, working capital, capex, term amortization, a ₹1 crore minimum cash floor, mutual-fund liquidation and ESOP exercise. All cases conservatively settle disclosed ₹0.3457 crore tax contingencies plus net opening income-tax payable of ₹0.0565 crore. No dividends are assumed; retained cash enters terminal equity once. The 142,000 granted options at ₹15 add ₹0.213 crore cash and dilute shares from 1.36 to 1.3742 crore once. The remaining 158,000 ungranted pool is not committed financing.
Conditional bear: 4% growth, an initial 10% sales shock, 9% EBIT margin and 10x exit EV/EBIT produce ₹75.19 and -6.42% IRR. Conditional base: 10% growth, 11.2% margin and 13x produce ₹177.03 and 11.05%. Conditional bull: 16% growth, 14% margin and 16x produce ₹362.89 and 28.20%. These cases are funded by existing resources assuming existing revolvers renew, not by new uncommitted borrowing. They are not probability-weighted forecasts.
The legal-adverse base adds a ₹7.0571 crore customs cash call plus an explicitly hypothetical ₹1 crore interest buffer; it remains funded and produces ₹171.16/10.31% IRR. The buffer is not a calculated legal liability. A persistent full remuneration-ceiling sensitivity produces ₹117.35/2.29%; continuation beyond the approved term is an assumption.
The 15% hurdle requires terminal price ₹210.79. At base operations that requires 15.53x exit EBIT instead of 13x. At 13x and 11.2% margin, the funded reverse model needs 14.15% growth and terminal revenue ₹201.30 crore. Conditional hurdle-entry arithmetic is ₹88.01, not a buy price before the gates clear. The full growth/margin/multiple grid is saved.
Control Print's FY26 group revenue/PAT are ₹481.96/₹43.60 crore versus Aztec ₹96.53/₹7.41 crore. Its official 19 October close was ₹587.25. A secondary share-count cross-check implies about ₹939.3 crore market value and 21.5x reported FY26 P/E. This is an indicative comparison, not a synchronized fully diluted EV benchmark. Official notes identify a ₹49.5769 crore FY25 MAT-credit benefit and FY26 exceptional subsidy; parent and group earnings differ. No misleading FY25 P/E or global-parent multiple median is used. The 10x/13x/16x exit range is an analyst sensitivity. [S1; M1–M4; P1–P6; model]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The linked stress combines an initial 15% revenue loss, 2% later growth, 8% EBIT margin, receivable days +30, inventory days +15, supplier days −10, capex cut to 2.5% of sales, 12% borrowing cost, a 10% mutual-fund haircut, a 25% revolver recall, and the customs cash-call/interest-buffer scenario. Tax contingencies and net opening income-tax payable are paid once. This is not a one-variable margin stress.
After existing mutual funds and lower discretionary capex, the peak minimum-cash funding gap is ₹10.30 crore. Ordinary terminal price, equity value and IRR are NULL. A hypothetical company cannot continue through an unfunded cash deficit and then deliver an ordinary positive return. This scenario is not an assertion of current insolvency or a verified presently payable customs claim.
A separate, uncommitted rescue issues ₹10.62 crore gross equity at a 40% discount to the entry quote and 3% fees. Terminal shares become 1.5431 crore, including ESOP, with ₹39.95 terminal price and -17.54% IRR for an existing nonparticipating holder. No filing commits investors to this funding. No extra money from the user is assumed. Restricted deposits and the corporate loan do not magically become available. Liquidation recovery is NS because recoverability and claim priority are not established.
The permanent-loss path is aged collections plus excess inventory, normalizing supplier credit, higher promoter costs and an adverse cash call while bank support tightens. Supplier nonrenewal would add another operational disruption. Counterweights are recurring consumables, positive operating earnings and the March bank regularization. The protection needed is verified legal and financing resolution, not a convenient exit rerating. [S1; S4–S9; model]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold/tenfold outcome from ₹104.80 means ₹524/₹1,048, requiring 37.97%/58.49% annual price appreciation over five years. The conditional base reaches only about 1.69x and the bull 3.46x after modeled cash, debt and dilution. A price multibagger is not interchangeable with revenue growth.
Keeping base cash, debt and diluted shares requires approximately ₹715 crore terminal EV for 5x and ₹1,435 crore for 10x, or about 39x and 78x base EBIT. Alternatively, a constant 13x operating multiple and 11.2% margin require a much larger revenue base and the working capital/capex to fund it. The separate reverse-growth check reports both the mathematical requirement and whether it survives the monthly funding test; an unfunded reverse-growth solution is not a plausible target.
An upside case would need renewed technology access, renewed hardware installations, larger active consumable cohorts, paying software deployments, stronger cash discipline and minority-friendly allocation. Neither company customer counts nor a global TAM establishes those outcomes. Neither 5x nor 10x is supported as a base expectation at this price. [S1; S4; S12; multibagger_checks.json]
At the fixed base margin and 13x multiple, the mathematical 5x/10x revenue CAGRs are 34.73%/52.35%, reaching ₹505.2/₹999.7 crore. Both paths are unfunded: peak gaps ₹60.6/₹189.3 crore. Their ordinary IRRs are NS.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Before any purchase conclusion, reconcile the customs appeal number, stay/payment status, High Court remand, interest calculation and the ₹0.50 crore deposit/refund. Ask for reconciliation with FY26 contingent notes without alleging concealment. Verify an executed Lead Tech renewal before the RHP's 6 December 2026 expiry, including territories, sales conditions, technology rights and pricing.
At the next half-year report, inspect printer units and ASP, active consumable customers, retention, normalized operating EBIT, warranty movements, cash before/after working capital, disputed/aged receivables and inventory obsolescence. Escalate if inventory and receivables outgrow sales or supplier credit reverses without replacement operating cash.
Track actual director pay against the ₹7 crore combined ceilings, related rents and Fluidtech/Axis settlement; ESOP grants/vesting; Jet's profit and cash returns; the ₹4.9449 crore corporate loan; commissioning/amortization of development assets; and bank facility renewal/collateral. An issuer letterhead saying 'CRISIL rated' is not a current verified rating rationale.
Implementation requires complete official BSE turnover, current ESM/ASM/GSM and trade-to-trade status, lot, circuit limits, spread and executable bid depth. ₹5 lakh is not an exact number of lots: four lots cost ₹4.192 lakh and five cost ₹5.24 lakh before fees. At 2%/5%/10% volume participation, only 4/9/17 of the 50 observed sessions allow at least one whole lot. Full-window median whole-lot capacity is zero even if all ten missing days were maximally liquid. No order or portfolio allocation follows automatically from this research. [S1; S4–S12; M1–M5]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: mixed-quality small industrial franchise with recurring consumables, not a verified high-quality compounder. BQS 4.94 (display 4.9), GQS 5.60 (display 5.6), IAS NS. BQS and GQS are conditionally rank-eligible because their factors are Medium confidence and G2 is Conditional, not Failed. IAS is not eligible. G3 Hold alone is not used to eliminate all quality rankings.
Research hold for fresh money. The conditional base does not meet the 15% hurdle, and unresolved claims, supplier continuity and execution data prevent a supported R/IAS. The close is not a promise that an existing holder can exit there; trading observations also do not justify calling the stock suspended.
Upgrade conditions: a reconciled legal position, executed supplier continuity, current exchange implementation checks, sustained hardware/consumables growth without cash deterioration, realized Jet returns and restrained actual promoter remuneration. Downgrade conditions: verified material unreliability or minority abuse, current unfunded liabilities, bank recall, supplier failure, unrecoverable aged assets or unsuccessful development. G2 failure would remove quality ranking eligibility; G1 failure or GOV≤3 would trigger the governance cap; actual G3 failure would cap a computable IAS at 3. [Evidence ledger]

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The primary packet includes audited FY24–FY26 reports, the 3 May 2024 RHP and restatements, Jet guarantee/bank filings, ESOP and AGM documents, AZTRACE launch material, the customs adjudication and the Supreme Court remand. Source locators and original downloads are retained. Evidence is labeled V for observations, C for calculations and E for estimates. No Git, Library or public writes were performed.
Material open questions remain: no H1FY27 balance sheet at the cutoff; no verified later customs merits/stay/payment/deposit/interest position; no executed Lead Tech renewal; current customer concentration, physical cohorts and capacity utilization unknown; primary latest pledge and surveillance data unverified; and ten missing sessions in secondary OHLCV history. The peer FY26 numeric table is a secondary reproduction because direct issuer downloads returned 403 and web table extraction was incomplete. Readable official peer notes confirm the tax distortion. No fully verified peer EV median is claimed.
The model assumes 25% tax, 10% ordinary debt cost, 12% stress cost, a ₹1 crore cash floor, 4.5% base capex and 2.3% D&A. Existing revolvers renew without new headroom. Term principal is amortized at ₹0.3522 crore/year, capped at ₹1.2622 crore; exact maturity dates remain unknown. Mutual funds are book-value liquidation assumptions, stressed separately, not guaranteed cash. Corporate-loan recovery and restricted-FD release are zero. ESOP cash/dilution is counted once; future employee-option expense must be absorbed within the assumed operating margin. Customs interest buffers, sustained pay-ceiling utilization and rescue equity are assumptions, not verified liabilities or commitments.
The deliverables are the canonical INE0SCB01016.json, aztec_model.json, monthly model CSV, financial history, growth drivers, legal reconciliation, liquidity rows/summary, peer checks, multibagger checks, source/read manifest and validation reports. The Python build and finalization scripts reproduce the outputs. This is deep, qualified research, not an assurance of returns.
